title: bn254-gt-dlp distinguished-point Pollard rho with tower-Karatsuba arithmetic

claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm in proof.md, with distinguished-point detection and tower-Karatsuba Fp12 arithmetic, can return x with g^x=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.50, using at most 2^129.928486 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) and at most 2^31 bytes of peak total storage. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic plus the quantified distinguished-point terms, supported and limited as explained in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. Total work includes all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, hashing, arithmetic, memory access, table lookups, recovery, verification and output. The uniform capped instruction bound is 2*ceil(sqrt(r))*87552+2^40, with all costs justified in machine.md. The walk, partition, and cap follow the track's rho-baseline-v2-20261110 package; the detection method and arithmetic are new to this package. No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or actual production-scale attack execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check full-width Montgomery and BN254 invariants, verify the tower/polynomial equality and Karatsuba operation counts, test the actual distinguished-point walk on small prime groups including failures, and reproduce the complete capped cost. These do not prove production success.
